title: Zacks: Brokerages Anticipate Apple (AAPL) Will Post Earnings of $2.19 Per Share
text:
Zacks: Brokerages Anticipate Apple (AAPL) Will Post Earnings of $2.19 Per Share Posted by Alanna Baker | Jun 7th, 2018
Brokerages expect that Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) will post earnings per share of $2.19 for the current quarter, according to Zacks . Eight analysts have made estimates for Apple’s earnings, with estimates ranging from $2.10 to $2.35. Apple posted earnings of $1.67 per share during the same quarter last year, which suggests a positive year-over-year growth rate of 31.1%. The firm is scheduled to announce its next earnings results on Tuesday, August 7th.
On average, analysts expect that Apple will report full year earnings of $11.43 per share for the current year, with EPS estimates ranging from $11.06 to $11.59. For the next fiscal year, analysts expect that the company will post earnings of $12.76 per share, with EPS estimates ranging from $11.08 to $13.84. Zacks’ earnings per share averages are an average based on a survey of sell-side research firms that follow Apple. Get Apple alerts:
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 EPS for the quarter, topping the consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. The company had revenue of $61.14 billion during the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $60.94 billion. Apple had a net margin of 21.55% and a return on equity of 39.97%. The company’s quarterly revenue was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. During the same quarter last year, the firm posted $2.10 EPS.
Several analysts have recently commented on AAPL shares. Barclays reduced their price objective on shares of Apple from $170.00 to $168.00 and set an “equal weight” rating for the company in a research report on Friday, March 16th. Morgan Stanley reduced their price objective on shares of Apple from $203.00 to $200.00 and set an “overweight” rating for the company in a research report on Friday, April 20th. Bank of America reaffirmed a “buy” rating and set a $220.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Friday, March 23rd. Vetr raised shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $184.49 price objective for the company in a research report on Monday, March 5th. Finally, Raymond James reiterated a “market perform” rating on shares of Apple in a report on Friday, February 16th. One analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-two have assigned a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the stock. Apple presently has a consensus rating of “Buy” and a consensus target price of $205.54.
In other news, COO Jeffrey E. Williams sold 15,653 shares of Apple stock in a transaction on Tuesday, May 8th. The stock was sold at an average price of $185.18, for a total transaction of $2,898,622.54. Following the sale, the chief operating officer now directly owns 168,181 shares in the company, valued at approximately $31,143,757.58. The transaction was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is available at the SEC website . Also, Director Arthur D. Levinson sold 35,000 shares of Apple stock in a transaction on Wednesday, May 9th. The stock was sold at an average price of $185.99, for a total value of $6,509,650.00. Following the sale, the director now owns 1,168,283 shares in the company, valued at $217,288,955.17. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last 90 days, insiders have sold 256,853 shares of company stock worth $45,378,566. Company insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock.
Several hedge funds and other institutional investors have recently added to or reduced their stakes in AAPL. Private Vista LLC increased its holdings in Apple by 267.1% in the 1st quarter. Private Vista LLC now owns 9,606 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $1,611,000 after acquiring an additional 6,989 shares during the last quarter. Altium Wealth Management LLC increased its holdings in Apple by 9.2% in the 1st quarter. Altium Wealth Management LLC now owns 24,638 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $4,134,000 after acquiring an additional 2,080 shares during the last quarter. Dundas Partners LLP purchased a new stake in Apple in the 1st quarter worth about $7,069,000. Nicola Wealth Management LTD. purchased a new stake in Apple in the 1st quarter worth about $5,470,000. Finally, Chesapeake Wealth Management purchased a new stake in Apple in the 1st quarter worth about $3,051,000. Institutional investors own 58.14% of the company’s stock.
Shares of AAPL stock traded down $0.64 during trading hours on Thursday, hitting $193.34. 9,824,503 shares of the company were exchanged, compared to its average volume of 20,524,124. The company has a market cap of $980.86 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 20.99, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.44 and a beta of 1.29. Apple has a fifty-two week low of $142.20 and a fifty-two week high of $194.08. The company has a quick ratio of 1.37, a current ratio of 1.46 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80.
Apple declared that its Board of Directors has authorized a stock repurchase plan on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to buyback $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This buyback authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to repurchase up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock buyback plans are generally an indication that the company’s management believes its shares are undervalued.
The business also recently disclosed a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Shareholders of record on Monday, May 14th were paid a dividend of $0.73 per share. The ex-dividend date of this dividend was Friday, May 11th. This is a boost from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.51%. Apple’s dividend payout ratio (DPR) is 31.70%.
Apple Company Profile
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. The company also sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.
